source_ref: Nam HJ, Yoon JY (2024) 'Pathways linking health literacy to self-care in diabetic patients with physical disabilities: A moderated mediation model', PLOS ONE 19(3):e0299971, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0299971 (CC BY 4.0). TEXT: The Washington Group Short Set on Functioning (WG-SS), official question document 19 March 2020, https://www.washingtongroup-disability.com/fileadmin/uploads/wg/Documents/Questions/Washington_Group_Questionnaire__1_-_WG_Short_Set_on_Functioning.pdf (sha256 73908cda00a88739a7ac67a7e698f418fd33ecc5f5354a1dab0c5edea970e423). MAPPING/VERIFICATION: article Methods paragraph 'Demographic and health-related characteristics' and Table 1 (journal.pone.0299971.t001, fetched as PNG and read directly) footnote b. ITEM CODES: S1 Data (journal.pone.0299971.s001, .xlsx, sheet Raw_Data), columns FL1..FL6. Processing script data/nam_2024_diabetes_battery.py. Cached under itemtext/.cache/nam_2024_function/.
note: mapping_basis=paper_order. data/nam_2024_diabetes_battery.py melts the S1 workbook's FL1..FL6 columns by name with no rename and no positional step (core-model derivation pattern 1), so the IRW item code IS the deposit column name -- but the deposit carries NO labels of any kind: the S1 .xlsx was opened this round, one sheet 'Raw_Data', 214 x 137, a bare ASCII header row, no variable or value labels, so there is no data_labels route and FL1..FL6 name nothing. What is inferred is domain order: the paper's Methods lists the six WG-SS domains in canonical order ('seeing, hearing, walking, remembering or concentrating, washing or dressing, and communicating') but ties them to no column code, so FLn -> nth canonical domain is presentation-order alignment. VERIFICATION: Step 5b routes 3/9 (option axis) + 8 + 5 (item axis), status PARTIAL, re-runnable as verify_nam_2024_function.R (VERDICT: PASS, 4/4 checks). Route 3/9 is decisive for the option axis: Table 1 reports Functional limitation Yes 135 (63.1%) / No 79 (36.9%) and footnote b defines Yes as reporting 'some difficulty', 'a lot of difficulty' or 'cannot do at all' in at least one domain; the live data give exactly 135 and 79, where a reversed scale would give 212. Routes 8 and 5 support the item axis: in this physically-disabled sample the two highest-difficulty items are FL3 (mean 1.930) and FL5 (1.822), the mobility and self-care domains; FL1-FL2 is the strongest correlation in the matrix (r=0.630, the seeing/hearing sensory pair) and FL3-FL6 the weakest (r=0.094, walking vs communicating). They do NOT separate FL1 from FL2, and FL4 vs FL6 rests only on an a-priori expectation (means 1.636 vs 1.668). TEXT: text_source=canonical_instrument, translation_source=official_instrument_english -- the wording is the Washington Group's own English question document (sha256 73908cda00a88739a7ac67a7e698f418fd33ecc5f5354a1dab0c5edea970e423), shipped in the base fields under the administered-language fallback because no Korean wording exists in the deposit or the paper's supplements (S1 Data is the only supplement). DEVIATIONS, all disclosed: the '[Do/Does] [you/he/she]' placeholders resolved to the self-report reading (self-administered online survey); the interviewer directive 'Would you say... [Read response categories]' omitted from item_text; response categories 7 'Refused' and 9 'Don't know' not shipped, since the processing script keeps only 1-4 and the live resp set is exactly {1,2,3,4}. correct_response blank -- a difficulty scale has no key. RIGHTS: no block. The WG-SS was developed and is disseminated by the Washington Group on Disability Statistics, a UN City Group; itemtext/instrument_rights_register.csv holds no matching row, and no fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause is quotable from the question document or the WG-SS question-set page. The one restriction-shaped sentence found is on the WG-SS FAQ page (https://www.washingtongroup-disability.com/resources/frequently-asked-questions/short-set/): 'In order to collect internationally comparable data, it is important that the WG question be used without any changes to the wording of questions, order of questions, response categories, and cut-off points for classification of disability.' That is methodological guidance about what the instrument is good for -- comparability of estimates -- and reserves no right, charges nothing and bars no redistribution, so under the 2026-09-08 LOT-R ruling it is quoted rather than treated as a block.
public_note: The survey was administered online in Korean and neither the article nor its S1 Data supplement publishes any Korean wording, so the item text shown here is the Washington Group's own canonical English WG-SS wording; the assignment of FL1-FL6 to the six domains follows the canonical WG-SS order that the paper's Methods reproduces, and the data confirm the mobility and self-care items (FL3, FL5) and the seeing/hearing pair (FL1, FL2) but cannot tell seeing from hearing.

note: Open-Source Psychometrics Project NPI-40 (openpsychometrics.org/_rawdata/NPI.zip). Forced-choice instrument: an item IS a pair of complete statements, so item_text is deliberately blank for all 40 items and both statements sit in option_text at resp=1 and resp=2 -- an encoding choice, not a coverage gap, and the reason audit_batch.R reports 100% blank item_text (expected, same shape as alsuhibani_2022_npi_s3 and eammi_grahe_2018_npi). MAPPING: the deposit's own codebook.txt keys every code and every stored value directly -- 'Q1. 1=I have a natural talent for influencing people. 2=I am not good at influencing people.' -- and data/narcissistic_personality_inventory.R does pivot_longer(Q1:Q40, names_to='item'), so the IRW item code IS the deposit column name (derivation pattern 1, no positional step). CORROBORATION: (a) the administered form at openpsychometrics.org/tests/NPI/1.php, fetched 2026-09-09, carries each statement inside <input name="Qk" value="v"> and matches the codebook 80/80 character for character, so the integer in resp is literally the value the chosen statement submitted; (b) per-item n in the live table equals the count of non-zero cells in the deposit column of the same name for 40/40 items (deposit total 448,298 = live rows 448,298); (c) recomputing the codebook's score formula from the raw Q columns reproduces the stored score for 11,243/11,243 respondents, confirming the 1/2 coding direction. VERSION (Step 3b): 40 items Q1-Q40 with resp in {1,2} is the NPI-40 forced-choice form, not the NPI-16/NPI-13; confirmed against the deposit itself rather than against the table name. INSTRUCTIONS transcribed verbatim from that live form ('For each pair of items choose the one that you most identify with. If you identify with both equally choose which one you think is most important.'); the data were collected earlier (deposit dated 2014) and no 2014 snapshot of the instruction line exists, but the 80 statements on the current form are byte-identical to the 2014 codebook. correct_response is blank: the NPI has no correct answer. The codebook does publish a keyed pole per item (the score formula above), which is a scoring key rather than a scoring key of correctness, so it is not shipped in correct_response. RIGHTS: no reserved right located. Raskin & Terry (1988, JPSP 54(5):890-902) state 'Free copies of the Narcissistic Personality Inventory are available to anyone who wishes to use it for research purposes' -- an offer, not a fee/permission/NC/ND/no-redistribution condition; the article's APA copyright line is a notice about the article (the PANAS case). The openpsychometrics test page's 'Your use of this assessment must be strictly for educational purposes. It can not be taken as psychological advice of any kind.' is a participation notice to test takers disclaiming fitness, quoted here per the LOT-R rule; it reserves nothing over the wording and openpsychometrics is not the rights holder. NPI-40 item text is already live in IRW as eammi_grahe_2018_npi. Not in instrument_rights_register.csv (no NPI row).

The 33 columns of the .sav (OSF u93eq, Codebooks, Data and Scripts/Study 1/Study 1 NAS.sav, 369 rows = the paper's N=369) are Age, Gender, Education plus the 30 adjectives abusive..egocentric, exactly the 30 item codes in the live table. The .sav carries NO variable labels and NO value labels (all 33 column labels are None, variable_value_labels is empty), so the words come from the study's own 'Study 1 Codebook.docx' in the same OSF folder, which lists the same 30 adjectives and the instructions verbatim; mapping is column-header identity, wording is the codebook. source_ref: Rogoza R, Baran L, Flakus M, Krammer G, Fatfouta R (2024). Introducing the Narcissistic Antagonism Scale: A missing puzzle piece in the assessment of momentary narcissism. Psychological Assessment. doi:10.1037/pas0001344. OSF project https://osf.io/u93eq (CC0 1.0): ITEM TEXT + INSTRUCTIONS + ANCHORS from 'Codebooks, Data and Scripts/Study 2/Study 2 Codebook.docx' (https://osf.io/download/vxjp3/); corroborating final-form wording from 'NAS - questionnaire and translations/NAS.xlsx' (https://osf.io/download/bp9yd/); VERIFICATION TARGET additional online Table 2 in 'Supplementary materials (Study 1 and Study 2).docx' (https://osf.io/download/ed6up/); RAW DATA 'Study 2 NAS.sav' (https://osf.io/download/cpb7q/); processing script data/nas_rogoza_2024.R
note: Item codes NAS1..NAS18 ARE the source column names: data/nas_rogoza_2024.R reads OSF u93eq's 'Study 2 NAS.sav', drops the NVS/NGS/NAS scale-score columns, pivots the remainder long with names_to='item', and filters grepl('NAS', item) -- no positional assignment and no rename. BUT the .sav carries NO variable labels and NO value labels (checked both levels: all 48 columns return NULL for attr 'label' and for attr 'labels'), so which adjective NAS7 holds is an ORDER inference off the study's own Study 2 Codebook.docx, hence mapping_basis=paper_order rather than data_labels. The codebook prints the administered instruction and then 42 adjectives in one unbroken list; the first 11 are exactly the 11 NVS adjectives, the next 18 the NAS pool and the last 13 the NGS adjectives, matching the .sav's NVS1-11 / NAS1-18 / NGS1-13 column blocks, and the paper's additional online Table 2 lists the same 42 adjectives in the same order. The first 16 of the 18 also match, in order, the 16 rows of the OSF 'NAS - questionnaire and translations/NAS.xlsx' final form; the two extra Study 2 items (Condescending, Selfish) are precisely the two the paper says cross-loaded onto the neurotic factor and were dropped, so the 18-item Study 2 pool is the 16-item final NAS plus those two. VERIFIED against the data per item, not merely per block: re-running the paper's 3-factor principal-axis oblimin EFA of all 42 adjectives with the LIVE IRW NAS responses substituted for the .sav's NAS columns reproduces additional online Table 2's published (Neurotic, Antagonistic, Agentic) triple for the adjective this extraction assigned to each code, worst euclidean deviation 0.021 over 18 items; all 18 published triples are mutually distinct (min separation 0.030) and nearest-neighbour matching recovers 18/18 code->adjective pairs (verify_nas_rogoza_2024_study2_nas.R). Deviations from literal transcription, all deliberate: (1) the codebook's instruction block ends 'Use the following scale to record your answers: 1 = Not at all 7 = Extremely'; the trailing anchor lines were moved out of `instructions` into `option_text` rather than recorded twice. (2) The scale labels only its endpoints, so option_text is populated for resp=1 ('Not at all') and resp=7 ('Extremely') and left blank for 2-6 -- the unlabelled points were NOT padded with their own numbers. (3) The instruction is the codebook's single instruction for the consolidated 42-adjective pool (the paper: 'All adjectives were consolidated into a unified item pool'), i.e. it is shared with the sibling nvs/ngs tables from this study; it is whole-table framing, so it sits in `instructions` and section_prompt is blank, with one trivial section_id. Study 2 was run on Prolific Academic with a sample representative of the American population (N=353), i.e. administered in English -- no language or _translated columns. RIGHTS: no clause reserves any right. The NAS is the source authors' own new instrument and they publish it themselves at https://osf.io/u93eq under CC0 1.0 Universal (OSF node license, verified via api.osf.io 2026-09-09), including a dedicated 'NAS - questionnaire and translations/NAS.xlsx' giving the English, Polish and German forms, the instruction and the response scale. That file's only condition-shaped text is 'Please cite as: Rogoza, R., Flakus, M., Baran, L., & Fatfouta, R. (2022). Development and validation of the Narcissistic Antagonism Scale.' -- a citation request, not a fee, permission, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution term. Not in instrument_rights_register.csv. The NVS and NGS adjectives are in the same source but are not this table's items.
